result.title: DirCast: Live Esports Directing and Commentary with a Single Streaming Video-Language Model
result.summary: A live esports broadcast needs a director who chooses which camera goes on air and a caster who talks over that choice, every second and without knowing what comes next. Streaming video language models have learned to commentate, but only over a broadcast that a human director has already produced. We study live broadcast production, in which a model receives the raw camera of every player and must both direct and commentate from the past alone. We present DirCast, a single streaming video language model that does both. Every second it scans all cameras at low resolution, decides with a hold-or-switch director whether and where to cut, and reads the chosen camera at high resolution before it speaks. Its context keeps what went on air and what was said and lets the other views expire, which bounds the cost of a stream of any length. We build a dataset of 27 professional Dota 2 matches with a camera for every hero, the human director's choices and the casters' commentary. DirCast directs better than rule-based and zero-shot directors including GPT-5, and its commentary wins 29.2 percent of comparisons against GPT-4o under the Proact-VL protocol, against 19.4 percent for the strongest of eleven streaming commentators that watch the human broadcast.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DirCast，一个流式视频语言模型，同时承担电竞赛事直播的导播与解说：每秒低分辨率扫描所有选手视角，由「hold-or-switch」策略决定是否切换机位，再对选中视角高分辨率读取后生成解说，并自建 27 场 Dota 2 比赛数据。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「低分辨率全扫→高分辨率读取选中视角→保持或切换」的流程与仅保留已播内容的上下文过期机制，可作为 LOOK/STOP、视觉证据筛选与动态计算成本界的可核查类比，但属任务级系统，未分析 latent 状态内容。
